#+TITLE: Hactar Modernization Plan — An AI-Era Harness
#+AUTHOR: Generated by pi
#+DATE: [2025-08-23]

* Vision

Hactar began (c. 2016) as a "solution to JavaScript Fatigue": a daemon that
watched your files, parsed your code, and ran plugins (sagas + reducers over a
CSP channel + Redux store) to install dependencies, wire up Babel, add
imports, and generate tests — all transparently, so your code never *depends*
on it.

The world moved: Vite/SWC/esbuild erased most build-config pain, TS became
default, and the new "fatigue" is *agent coordination* — keeping a project's
substrate coherent while humans *and* AI coding agents mutate it
continuously. Agents today operate one-shot: they edit, run a command, read
output, edit again. There is no persistent, deterministic, auditable layer
that reacts to mutations, enforces conventions, keeps the toolchain current,
and feeds structured state back to the agent.

Hactar 2.0 is that layer: **a long-running project harness that AI agents
plug into.** It is the deterministic automation and verification substrate
under the reasoning agent.

- Agents reason; Hactar reacts.
- Agents edit; Hactar keeps the build green, deps installed, configs current,
  conventions enforced via codemods, and diagnostics published.
- Agents connect via MCP; Hactar exposes the project's live state, an event
  stream, a codemod engine, a capability registry, and a diagnostics bus.
- Agents can *author plugins on the fly* to automate a recurring task;
  Hactar hot-loads them. Plugins are the unit of "teach the harness a new
  reflex."

The original thesis survives, sharpened: *stay out of your way, be massively
hackable, do not become a dependency, lots of small wins.* The realization
changes: a human-typed file save and an agent-applied patch are the same
event, and the harness serves both.

* What hactar was → what it becomes

| Dimension         | Hactar 1 (2016)                      | Hactar 2 (AI era)                              |
|-------------------+-------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------|
| Purpose           | Cure JS build-config fatigue         | Deterministic harness/co-pilot for AI agents  |
| Consumers         | A human coding in an editor          | Humans + AI coding agents (via MCP)           |
| Mutation source   | =chokidar= file events               | File events *and* agent actions (MCP tools)    |
| Plugin authorship  | Human writes npm package             | Human *or agent* writes ephemeral/hot plugin  |
| Effects           | =execSync('npm install')= inline     | Declared effects, executed by core, replayable|
| State             | Redux store, un-namespaced           | Namespaced slices + event log, queryable     |
| Diagnostics       | =console.log=                        | Diagnostics bus → channel + MCP subscription  |
| Codemods          | Left to plugins (jscodeshift)        | First-class =ast-grep= engine as an effect    |
| Config of truth   | =.babelrc= era                       | =tsconfig=/=vite.config= era; Hactar adapts   |
| Surface           | CLI only                            | CLI daemon + MCP server (stdio + HTTP)        |
| Deps              | Babel 6, =js-csp=, =chalk@1=, etc.   | Native ESM, zero abandoned deps              |

* Updated principles

1. *Stay out of the way.* Hactar never blocks the agent or human; it reacts
   in the background and only surfaces results through a diagnostics bus the
   consumer subscribes to.
2. *Be massively hackable — by agents too.* A plugin is a small module an
   agent can write and Hactar can hot-load in one round-trip. The barrier to
   "teach the harness a reflex" is a function, not an ecosystem.
3. *Do not become a dependency.* Everything Hactar writes is plain project
   config/code. Removing Hactar leaves a working, conventional project.
4. *Determinism under the agent.* Effects are *declared*, not executed
   inline, so a plugin's behavior is testable, replayable, and introspectable
   by the agent (the agent can ask "what would this plugin do?" without
   running it).
5. *Small wins, continuously.* Each plugin ships one reflex. The harness
   compounds them; the agent doesn't have to re-derive them every session.

* Architecture

** Process model
- A single daemon process (=hactar= run in a project root), lifecycle-managed
  (foreground, =--daemon=, or via a host editor/agent).
- Core loop:
  1. =chokidar= (v4) emits FS events.
  2. Events are normalized into Flux-standard actions
     ({type, payload, meta:{source:'fs'|'agent'|'plugin'}}).
  3. Actions go on an in-tree async channel (=src/channel.js=).
  4. A =pluginRunner= drains the channel, runs reducer slices, and spawns
     saga handlers with an =api= object.
  5. Sagas declare effects; the core's =effectRunner= executes them
     (install dep, write file, run command, run codemod, emit diagnostic).
  6. All actions + effects are appended to an append-only event log.

** Plugin protocol (v2)
A plugin is an ES module exporting any of:

#+begin_src js
export const init   = async (api) => {}            // once, at startup
export const reducer = (sliceState, action, api) => sliceState // namespaced
export const saga   = async function* (action, api) {} // per-action; generator OR
export const saga   = async (action, api) => {}        // plain async fn
#+end_src

=api= provides:
- =put(action)=, =take()=, =close()= — channel ops (promise-returning; a
  tiny =js-csp=-compatible shim is re-exported from =hactar/csp= for legacy
  plugins that =import { put } from 'js-csp'=).
- =getState(name?)= — namespaced state slice (or whole state).
- =dispatch(action)= — synchronous store dispatch.
- =spawn(fn)= — long-running coroutine with cancel token (for =init=).
- Effects (declared, returned/yielded, executed by core):
  =exec(cmd,opts)=, =installDeps(pkgs)=, =writeFile(path, content)=,
  =applyCodemod(rule, transform)=, =runChecks(scope)=,
  =emitDiagnostic(diag)=, =mcpTool(name, args)=.
- =mcp= — publish/subscribe to the MCP surface (see below).

** Effect discipline
Effects are *values*, not side-effects inline. A saga yields/returns
={type:'exec', cmd:'jest', args:['--watch']=}=; the core executes it and
returns the result. Consequences:
- Plugins are unit-testable without touching the FS or shell.
- An agent can dry-run a plugin ("plan mode") by collecting its declared
  effects without executing.
- The event log is a faithful replay transcript.
- Concurrency/cancellation live in one place (the core), with debouncing for
  installs and a per-project command queue.

** MCP server (=src/mcp.js=)
Implements Model Context Protocol (stdio for local agents, optional HTTP/SSE
for remote). Exposes:
- *Tools* (agent-invocable):
  - =run_codemod=, =install_dependency=, =write_file=,
    =run_checks= (test/typecheck/lint/build, scoped),
    =get_diagnostics=, =subscribe_events=, =load_plugin=,
    =list_capabilities=, =replay_session=.
- *Resources* (read-only live state):
  - =project://state= — current store snapshot.
  - =project://deps=, =project://diagnostics=, =project://event-log=,
    =project://plugins=.
- *Prompts*:
  - =summarize-drift= ("what changed since the agent last looked?"),
    =propose-fix= (given diagnostics, suggest a codemod or patch),
    =explain-capability= ("how do I run tests here?").

The channel is bridged to MCP subscriptions: an agent calls
=subscribe_events= and receives a live stream of normalized actions and
diagnostics — the same stream plugins see.

** Codemod engine
First-class =applyCodemod= effect backed by =ast-grep= (fast, multi-language,
pattern-based) with an optional =ts-morph=/jscodeshift path for TypeScript
type-aware transforms. Plugins ship =.sgy= rule files or transform functions;
agents can submit ad-hoc transforms. This replaces the old "left to plugins,
figure it out yourself" approach with a shared, inspectable facility.

** Capability registry
Plugins register capabilities they *provide* (e.g. =test-runner=,
=build-system=, =lint=, =format=) keyed to project signals. An agent asks
=list_capabilities= and gets a resolved answer ("jest is the test runner;
command is =npm test="). This is the modern replacement for hactar 1's
"parse imports and guess" — explicit, queryable, and agent-friendly.

** Diagnostics bus
Aggregates from: effect =runChecks=, plugin =emitDiagnostic=, and a watcher
on the project's existing tooling output files. Publishes normalized
={severity, source, file, range, message}= records to the channel and to
the MCP =project://diagnostics= resource. Agents subscribe and react.

* Phased Plan

Each phase leaves a runnable CLI/daemon.

** Phase 0 — Repo hygiene (mechanical)
- [ ] Create =bin/hactar.js= with shebang, =chmod +x=, fix =package.json=
  =bin=. (Currently points at nonexistent =./bin/index.js=.)
- [ ] Add =type: "module"=, =engines: { node: ">=20" }=, =files= allowlist;
  delete =.npmignore=.
- [ ] Add =.nvmrc=, =.gitattributes=, lockfile (after Phase 2 trim).

** Phase 1 — Drop Babel 6; ship native ESM
- [ ] Delete =.babelrc=; remove =babel-cli=, =babel-polyfill=,
  =babel-preset-es2015=, =babel-preset-stage-0=.
- [ ] Rewrite =src/index.js= as ESM; remove =import 'babel-polyfill'=.
- [ ] Drop =build= script and =lib/= entry; =main= → =src/index.js=; remove
  =lib/= from =.gitignore=.
- [ ] Replace =docpress= (dead) with GitHub-rendered =docs/= or VitePress.

** Phase 2 — Upgrade/replace dependencies
| Old dep           | Replacement                          |
|-------------------+--------------------------------------|
| =babel-polyfill=  | (native JS)                          |
| =chalk@1=         | =picocolors=                         |
| =chokidar@1=      | =chokidar@4=                         |
| =commander@2=     | =commander@13=                       |
| =redux@3=         | =redux@5= (or an in-tree 20-LOC store; Redux is optional once state is namespaced slices) |
| =js-csp@0.5=      | in-tree async channel (Phase 3a)     |
| =gitignore-globs= | =ignore@6=                           |
| =classnames=      | remove (unused)                      |
| =hactar-util=     | vendor the helper or pin real ver    |

- [ ] AirBNB ESLint (v6-era) → flat =eslint.config.js= with =@eslint/js=
  recommended + =eslint-plugin-import=; drop =eslint-plugin-react=;
  =ecmaVersion 2024=, =sourceType: module=.

** Phase 3 — Core runtime rework (the harness foundation)
- [ ] *3a.* =src/channel.js=: ~40-LOC unbounded async FIFO channel
  (=put/take/close/CLOSE=). Re-export a =js-csp=-compatible =put/take/chan=
  shim as =hactar/csp= for legacy plugins.
- [ ] *3b.* Plugin loading via dynamic =import()=; scan
  =dependencies/devDependencies/peerDependencies= matching
  =/^hactar-[-\w]+/=. Hot-reload =hactar.config-plugin.js= and
  agent-loaded plugins (cache-bust via =?t= query or process restart).
- [ ] *3c.* Saga API: accept =async function=, =async function*=, or legacy
  generator; auto-iterate generators. Add =init(api)= lifecycle for
  long-running loops (fixes the README-promised-but-unimplemented "run on a
  loop"). Provide =spawn(fn)= with cancellation.
- [ ] *3d.* Namespaced reducer slices keyed by plugin name; =getState(name)=.
  Top-level state reserved for core (=config=, =ignored=, =plugins=,
  =capabilities=, =diagnostics=).
- [ ] *3e.* Effect system: effects are values; =src/effects.js= executes them
  with a per-project queue, debounce on installs, cancellation tokens.
  Replace =execSync('npm install')= with a declared =installDeps= effect run
  via =child_process.spawn=, piped to =stdout/stderr=, non-blocking. Detect
  =pnpm/yarn/npm= from lockfile.
- [ ] *3f.* Event log: append-only =src/log.js= writing JSONL to
  =.hactar/session.jsonl=; supports =replay_session=.

** Phase 4 — Codemod engine + capability registry
- [ ] =src/codemod.js=: =applyCodemod= effect wrapping =ast-grep= (rule
  files under =codemods/*.sgy= or inline transforms); optional
  =ts-morph= path for type-aware TS transforms.
- [ ] =src/capabilities.js=: plugins declare
  =provides: { role: 'test-runner', detect, command }=; registry resolves
  on demand and publishes to =project://capabilities= resource.
- [ ] =src/diagnostics.js=: bus collecting =runChecks= results + plugin
  diagnostics; normalized records published to channel + MCP resource.

** Phase 5 — MCP server
- [ ] =src/mcp.js= implementing MCP (stdio; optional HTTP/SSE transport).
  Tools, resources, prompts per Architecture section.
- [ ] Bridge channel → =subscribe_events= MCP subscription (live action +
  diagnostic stream to agents).
- [ ] =--mcp= flag on the CLI to run *only* the MCP server against a shared
  =.hactar/session.jsonl= (so a host agent can attach without forking the
  watcher), and =--serve= to run daemon + MCP together.

** Phase 6 — Tests + CI
- [ ] =node --test= suite:
  - =test/channel.test.js=, =test/effects.test.js= (declared-effect
    execution + replay), =test/reducer.test.js= (namespacing),
  - =test/plugins.test.js= (discovery + hot-load), =test/codemod.test.js=,
  - =test/capabilities.test.js=, =test/mcp.test.js= (in-process MCP client),
  - =test/cli.test.js= (spawn =bin/hactar.js= in temp =cwd= with a fixture
    plugin; assert boot/watch/dispatch).
- [ ] =test= script: =node --test=; =--watch= mode.
- [ ] =.github/workflows/ci.yml=: =npm ci && npm run lint && npm test= on
  Node 20 & 22, linux/mac/win.
- [ ] Release workflow: single source of truth for version (=import =
  =../package.json= with { type:'json' }= → =program.version=); delete
  hardcoded ="0.0.5"=. =.changeset= or =CHANGELOG.md=.

** Phase 7 — Docs & positioning refresh
- [ ] Reposition README from "JS Fatigue cure" to "deterministic harness for
  AI coding agents." Keep the four original principles; add *determinism
  under the agent*.
- [ ] Document plugin v2 API (async, =api= object, declared effects, =init=,
  namespaced =getState=, capabilities, codemod registration) with
  side-by-side legacy↔modern examples.
- [ ] MCP section: tool/resource/prompt catalog for agent integrators.
- [ ] Agent cookbook: "how an agent writes and hot-loads a plugin,"
  "subscribe to diagnostics," "propose + dry-run a codemod."
- [ ] Replace dead links (Gratipay, Cash.me, Dropbox screencast).

* Risk register
- *Breaking legacy =hactar-*= plugins (=hactar-babel=, =hactar-auto-install=
  use generator + =yield put(ch, ...)=). Mitigation: auto-iterate
  generators in 3c; =hactar/csp= compat shim; bump core to =1.0.0= to
  signal the break; provide a =--legacy-plugin-mode= that wraps old sagas.
- *ESM has no =require.cache=* → hot-reload semantics change. Mitigation:
  restart-on-save for =hactar.config-plugin.js=, or a worker-process sandbox
  per plugin group. Document explicitly.
- *=js-csp= removal* surprises vendored plugins. Mitigation: =hactar/csp=
  shim re-exporting =put/take/chan/CLOSE= with identical call shapes.
- *MCP surface churn* — the protocol is young. Mitigation: pin a MCP SDK
  version; isolate transport behind =src/mcp.js=.
- *Effect determinism vs. real-world side effects* (a codemod touches
  files). Mitigation: dry-run/plan mode returns the *would-be* effect set;
  mutations gate behind =apply= confirmation for agent-submitted codemods
  unless =--trust-agent= is set.
- *chokidar 4* dropped some v1 options. Audit our =ignored= (regex/array →
  function matcher).

* Out of scope / future
- TypeScript core rewrite (keep JS + JSDoc + =ts.check= for now).
- LSP server (Hactar-as-language-server) — MCP covers the agent path; LSP is
  a later, thinner adapter over the same diagnostics bus.
- A plugin discovery registry/site.
- Multi-project/monorepo orchestration beyond a single =cwd=.
- Built-in agent loop (Hactar intentionally stays *non*-agentic — it is the
  substrate, not the reasoner).

* Definition of done
- =npm i -g hactar= yields a working =hactar= binary; =--version= reads from
  =package.json=.
- =hactar= in a temp dir boots, loads a fixture plugin, watches, and
  dispatches =ADD_FILE= / =CHANGED_FILE= via declared effects (no
  =execSync=).
- =hactar --mcp= speaks MCP over stdio; a scripted MCP client can
  =list_tools=, =subscribe_events=, =run_codemod=, and =get_diagnostics=.
- An agent-authored plugin can be hot-loaded at runtime and its declared
  effects dry-run (plan mode) before execution.
- =npm test= green on Node 20 & 22 in CI; zero abandoned dependencies
  (=js-csp=, =gitignore-globs=, =babel-polyfill=, =docpress= all gone); no
  Babel step.
- README + docs reflect the harness vision, plugin v2 API, and MCP surface.

* Suggested PR order
1. Phase 0 — hygiene + =bin= fix (unblocks any release on its own).
2. Phase 1 — drop Babel (small, big DX win).
3. Phase 2 — dep upgrades (mechanical; careful =src/index.js= edits).
4. Phase 3 — core rework: channel + effect system + namespacing + init
   (the substantive change; commits 3a–3f).
5. Phase 4 — codemod engine + capabilities + diagnostics bus.
6. Phase 5 — MCP server (builds on 3 & 4).
7. Phase 6 — tests (drafted alongside 3–5) + CI.
8. Phase 7 — docs/positioning (after API + MCP surface are frozen).
